'''C2''' is the sixth and highest level of the [[CEFR The Common European Framework of Reference for Languages|Common European Framework]] and the upper '''Proficient User''' level. Its informal name is '''Mastery'''.

== What C2 actually means ==

A C2 speaker can understand with ease '''virtually everything heard or read'''. They can summarise information from different spoken and written sources, reconstructing arguments and accounts in a coherent presentation. They can express themselves spontaneously, very fluently and precisely, '''differentiating finer shades of meaning''' even in more complex situations.

== What C2 is not ==

'''C2 does not mean "native speaker", and the framework does not say it does.''' This is the most persistent misunderstanding about the scale, and it runs in both directions:

* Many highly educated native speakers would '''not''' pass a C2 examination without preparation, because the examination tests summarising, register control and precision under timed conditions — skills that are taught, not inherited.
* A C2 certificate holder may still have an accent, gaps in idiom, or unfamiliarity with regional varieties. None of that is what the level measures.

C2 describes '''what a person can do with the language''', which is the design principle of the whole framework. It is a ceiling on the scale, not a claim about origin.

== What it is worth in practice ==

* '''Academic and professional.''' Translation, interpreting, editing, publication, teaching the language itself, and senior roles where precision carries consequences.
* '''Teaching.''' For a non-native teacher of a language, a C2 certificate is the credential that settles the question before it is asked.
* '''Study.''' Exceeds the requirement of essentially every institution, which is why relatively few people take it for admission purposes. People take C2 because they want the ceiling.

== Certificates at C2 with staying power ==

* '''English''' — '''C2 Proficiency''', the '''Certificate of Proficiency in English''', '''first introduced in 1913'''. It is the oldest examination in the Cambridge suite — the first one the organisation ever developed — and among the oldest language certificates still in use anywhere in the world. It was substantially revised in the late 1990s with the revised version launched in '''December 2002'''. A certificate with a continuous history of more than a century is the strongest possible answer to the question of whether a credential will still mean something in twenty years.
* '''Spanish''' — '''DELE C2''', Instituto Cervantes.
* '''French''' — '''DALF C2''', French Ministry of Education. Lifetime diploma.
* '''German''' — '''Goethe-Zertifikat C2: Großes Deutsches Sprachdiplom''', Goethe-Institut.
* '''Italian''' — '''CILS Quattro C2''', '''CELI 5''', '''PLIDA C2'''.

== How long it takes ==

Estimates past C1 become unreliable and most published figures stop there. Reaching C2 generally requires '''years of sustained use''' in the language — reading widely, writing for readers, working in it — rather than a countable number of class hours. It is the one level that cannot really be bought as a course.

== Where to go next ==

Nowhere on this scale; C2 is the top of it. The remaining direction is '''sideways, into registers''' — business, legal, medical, religious, technical. A C2 speaker is a beginner in any register they have never worked in, which is the point made at [[Language Registers Business Religious and Trade Language]].
